subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should native backup exclusion support land now, and if so should the core CLI include smart defaults and automatic `.backupignore` loading or only explicit user-supplied patterns?
rationale: The implementation changes a recovery-critical CLI contract: defaults, trusted local ignore files, protected paths, and external asset behavior affect both sensitive data exposure and whether backups remain restorable.

options.title: Rebase and review as canonical
options.body: Use this PR or a maintainer rewrite as the canonical path, but require current-main integration, opt-in/default decisions, external-asset semantics, real behavior proof, and security review before merge.

options.title: Narrow to explicit excludes first
options.body: Accept only repeatable `--exclude` and explicit `--exclude-file` support while deferring smart defaults and automatic `.backupignore` discovery until restore/security expectations are settled.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Keep core backup scope coarse for now, document the current limits, and leave optional backup strategies to plugins or ClawHub after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Rebase and review as canonical
recommendation.body: Use this PR or a maintainer rewrite as the canonical path, but require current-main integration, opt-in/default decisions, external-asset semantics, real behavior proof, and security review before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the original backup CLI review/merge and adjacent backup infra extraction, making them the best routing candidate for the core backup contract choice.
